paraphrase: 'The sky is thick with clouds, the woods dark with tamāla trees; he is afraid of the night — Rādhā, take him home.' So bidden by Nanda, Rādhā and Mādhava go, and on the bank of the Yamunā their secret loves triumph.
speaker: Jayadeva (narrator)

paraphrase: The hymn of the ten avatāras: O Keśava, taking the body of the fish you held the Veda in the waters of dissolution; as tortoise you bore the earth; as boar, man-lion, dwarf, Paraśurāma, Rāma, Balarāma; as the Buddha, with a compassionate heart you condemned the Vedic ordinance of sacrifice that showed the killing of animals; as Kalki you will destroy the barbarians — victory to you, Hari, lord of the world. The closing verse offers homage to Kṛṣṇa who takes these ten forms.
speaker: Jayadeva
notes: Refrain 'keśava dhṛta-...-śarīra jaya jagadīśa hare'. Kṛṣṇa is the avatārin (source), Balarāma the eighth form. Canto-level ref; verse numbering within cantos differs between editions.

paraphrase: In the lovely spring, when soft breezes from Malaya stir the clove creepers and the bees and cuckoos sing, Hari plays here, dancing with the young women — a time hard to bear for those in separation.

paraphrase: Dark body anointed with sandal, yellow-robed, garlanded with forest flowers, Hari sports with the throng of charmed cowherd women, embracing one, kissing another, gazing at another; Rādhā's friend shows her the sight.

notes: Refrain 'harir iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilasati keli-pare'. The rāsa of the Bhāgavata (10.29–33) in Jayadeva's form. Canto-level ref; verse numbering within cantos differs between editions.

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa pleads with Rādhā to give up her anger: 'if you speak even a little, the moonlight of your teeth dispels my fearful darkness ... place on my head, as its ornament, your generous foot-blossom, which destroys the poison of love.'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: 'smara-garala-khaṇḍanaṃ mama śirasi maṇḍanaṃ dehi pada-pallavam udāram'. The tradition's account: Jayadeva hesitated to write that the Lord asks for Rādhā's foot on his head; while he bathed, Kṛṣṇa in his form wrote the line himself (phn:jayadeva-line-written-by-krsna). paraphrase: Whatever skill there is in the arts of music, whatever meditation on Viṣṇu, whatever discernment of the truth of love and whatever play in poetry — let the joyful wise learn it all from the Gīta Govinda of the learned poet Jayadeva, whose self is wholly intent on Kṛṣṇa. May the poetry of the Gīta Govinda of Jayadeva, son of Bhojadeva and Rāmādevī, be on the lips of Parāśara and his other dear friends.
speaker: Jayadeva
